chunks: In fact, great concern (i.e., fear) has made them mad.
They are not satisfied with their meagre good acts, and do not regard their major acts as great. They always blame themselves and are afraid of their deeds.
When anyone of them is spoken of highly, he says: “I know myself better than others, and my Lord knows me better than I know.
O Allāh, do not deal with me according to what they say, and make me better than they think of me and forgive me (those shortcomings) which they do not know.”
ai.seo_question: What are the psychological and spiritual characteristics of the God-fearing according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) illustrates the profound spiritual anxiety of the God-fearing, who view their deeds as insufficient and remain vigilant against the corruption of praise. This passage highlights the dialectic between self-knowledge and divine omniscience, where the believer’s humility leads to a constant supplication for forgiveness of what others do not see. In Shia tradition, this reflects the concept of *muhasaba* (self-accounting) as a prerequisite for spiritual elevation.
